activities.name: Kuruva Island boardwalk walk – gentle 2 km trail on elevated planks, perfect for a relaxed first day and easy on the eyes

meals.breakfast: At hotel – South‑Indian spread (idiyappam, coconut chutney, fresh fruit)

lunch.description: Kerala thali with steamed rice, sambar, avial and banana chips, enjoyed under the shade of Kuruva’s bamboo groves
lunch.location_note: near Kuruva Island — approx 12 km from Kalpetta hotel

dinner.description: Kerala style fish curry with appam – local specialty
Vegetarian thali (rice, dal, vegetable stir‑fry, papad) at a family‑run eatery in Kalpetta
Fine‑dining restaurant serving Malabar biryani with saffron‑infused rice and grilled prawns, candle‑lit ambience

days.notes: Arrive at Calicut Airport, pick up a monsoon‑ready SUV and drive ~2 hrs to Kalpetta. Keep the first day light to recover from travel; afternoon rest at hotel is optional.

activities.name: Guided morning safari in Tholpetty Wildlife Sanctuary – 2‑hour jeep ride with a certified naturalist, spotting elephants, deer and birds

meals.breakfast: At hotel – warm dosas with coconut chutney and sambar

lunch.description: Kerala chicken stew with appam, served at a dhaba near the sanctuary entrance
lunch.location_note: near Tholpetty Sanctuary entrance — approx 18 km from Kalpetta hotel

dinner.description: Prawn roast with neer dosa – coastal flavor close to Wayanad’s backwaters
Paneer butter masala with naan at a popular family restaurant in Kalpetta
Upscale garden terrace dinner featuring smoked duck breast with Kerala spices

days.notes: Leave Kalpetta by 7:00 AM to reach the sanctuary before the mid‑day heat. Carry raincoats; monsoon showers are common. Evening at hotel – optional spa for relaxation.

activities.name: Edakkal Caves trek – 3 km ascent with stone steps, guided by a local expert (check opening status early morning). If closed, replace with a serene boat ride on Pookode Lake.

meals.breakfast: At hotel – fresh fruit salad, boiled eggs, and filter coffee

lunch.description: Rice bowl with fish curry and a side of thoran (stir‑fried vegetables)
lunch.location_note: near Edakkal Caves (or Pookode Lake) — approx 25 km from Kalpetta hotel

dinner.description: Malabar chicken biryani with raita – aromatic and hearty
Vegetarian thali (steamed rice, dal, vegetable curries, pickle) at a well‑reviewed family eatery
Premium lakeside dining with grilled salmon, herb‑infused butter, and a view of the sunset over the water

days.notes: Monsoon can make the cave steps slippery; verify open status the night before. Carry a torch, waterproof shoes and a rain poncho. If the caves are closed, the Pookode Lake boat ride offers a safe, scenic alternative.

activities.name: Morning tea‑estate walk – leisurely stroll through a tea plantation with a brief talk on organic tea processing (flat terrain, <20 min walk)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – traditional Kerala appam with sweet banana stew

lunch.description: Light vegetable pulao with cucumber raita, eaten at a roadside dhaba before departure
lunch.location_note: on NH 766, approx 10 km from Kalpetta hotel

dinner.description: No dinner scheduled – departure for Calicut Airport in the afternoon

days.notes: Check out by 11:00 AM, enjoy the tea‑estate walk, then drive to Calicut International Airport (≈2 hrs). Allow extra time for monsoon‑related road checks.

warnings: August is heavy monsoon season – expect frequent landslides on NH 766; keep a flexible schedule and monitor local traffic updates.
Edakkal Caves are often closed in monsoon due to safety concerns; confirm opening status the night before and have Pookode Lake as a fallback.
Leeches are common in wet forest trails; wear long trousers and apply insect repellent.
Unauthorized vendors may sell ‘cave lighting kits’; bring your own torch or join an official guided trek (₹200 per person).

Edakkal Caves involve a 3 km steep climb with uneven stone steps; not suitable for toddlers or elderly with limited mobility. Mitigation: assess fitness, use proper trekking shoes, start early (6‑9 am) to avoid heat and crowds.

Monsoon (June‑September) makes the trail slippery and the caves are officially closed due to safety concerns. Mitigation: avoid trekking during heavy rain, check local updates, and consider lower‑elevation walks if visiting in August.

Landslides are frequent on NH 766 during monsoon, potentially blocking the approach route. Mitigation: monitor road conditions, allow extra travel time, and have an alternate route via Mysore‑Gundlupet if needed.

Unauthorized vendors sell ‘cave lighting’ kits at ₹500 each, claiming they are required. Mitigation: carry a personal torch or join an official guided trek (₹200 per person) where lighting is provided.
Verify whether Edakkal Caves are open before setting out; monsoon closures are common.
Carry rain gear, insect repellent (leeches are prevalent), and a basic medical kit.
If trekking in moderate pace, consider hiring a local guide (₹200 per person) for safety and navigation.
Ensure vehicle is monsoon‑ready (good tires, brakes) and keep emergency contacts for landslide‑prone stretches.
As a fallback, explore easier trails such as the Kuruva Island boardwalk or guided walks in Tholpetty Sanctuary, which remain accessible during monsoon.
personalization_notes: Couple‑focused itinerary balances nature immersion (wildlife safari, cave trek) with relaxed evenings for quality time.
Mid‑range budget tier kept in mind – activities and meals chosen to offer authentic Kerala experiences without premium price spikes.
Moderate pace respects your preference for comfortable travel days while still covering Wayanad’s top natural highlights.
